title: PostgreSQL Indexing: The Definitive Guide to B-Tree, GIN, and GiST
content:
# PostgreSQL Indexing Deep Dive

When scaling relational databases, proper indexing is often the single highest leverage performance optimization. B-Trees excel at range queries and equality comparisons. GIN (Generalized Inverted Index) is unmatched for full-text search and JSONB containment queries.

### Key Rules:
1. Index foreign keys to avoid full table locks on cascade deletions.
2. Use partial indexes (WHERE condition) to keep indexes compact.
3. Monitor pg_stat_user_indexes for dead/unused index bloat.
note: Essential reference for tuning queries and designing multi-tenant schemas.
summary: Comprehensive breakdown of PostgreSQL index types: B-Tree for equality/ranges, GIN for JSONB and full-text search, and tips for partial indexing to reduce bloat.

title: Building Modern Chrome Extensions with Manifest V3 and Side Panel API
content:
# Manifest V3 & The Chrome Side Panel API

Manifest V3 shifts background pages to ephemeral service workers and introduces dedicated side panels via chrome.sidePanel. This enables continuous contextual interactions alongside the user's active browsing session.

### Architectural Insights:
- Use storage.sync for small user preferences (<100KB).
- Offload heavy DOM parsing to content scripts.
- Keep service workers stateless to handle background lifecycle suspensions.
note: Guide used to architect OmniClip companion extension.
summary: Covers Chrome MV3 side panel lifecycle, background service worker constraints, and cross-context message passing patterns.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Chunking Strategies & Vector Search
content:
# Effective RAG Architecture

Naively chunking documents by character count destroys semantic coherence. Modern RAG pipelines implement recursive character splitting with overlap or sentence window retrieval. Pairing vector cosine distance with reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) delivers the highest retrieval accuracy.
note: Must read before setting up our pgvector search pipeline.
summary: Explains why semantic chunking and hybrid search (BM25 + Dense Vectors) outperform naive text chunking in LLM document retrieval systems.
